Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Helpful walkthrough — a few follow-ups from our side as we try to size this out for our security/compliance review and budget planning: 

- Expected token volumes: we estimate 80M prompt tokens + 150M completion tokens per month initially (peak 300M total/month in 6–9 months).
- Budget range: leadership gave a $100k–$180k annual budget target for inference licensing and support for the first year.
- Our preference is a Private/VPC deployment behind our VPC with customer-managed KMS. We need a clear licensing model (per-environment? per-GPU?), expected unit economics, and target $/1M tokens so we can compare against other options.

Also, please confirm what support tiers mean for SLA and whether we can have 2 non-prod environments + 1 prod environment.

Can you send a short follow-up with ballpark numbers and recommended configuration so we can take it into our procurement loop?

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@medlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priya.sharma@medlytics.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — pricing follow-up

Jordan — great talking earlier. Short follow-up / recap and a few clarifying q's so the numbers below map correctly to your environment: 

Recap of what we have so far:
- Month 0 volumes: ~230M total tokens/month (80M prompt + 150M completion).
- Expected peak: ~300M tokens/month in 6–9 months.
- Deployment: Private (VPC) behind your KMS. Request: 2 non-prod + 1 prod environments.

Quick clarifying Qs:
1) Is the 300M/month an expected steady-state or occasional peak? (matters for burst vs reserved capacity).
2) Do you expect a large percentage of cache hits/prefix caching (e.g., >30%)? That affects effective unit tokens.

Ballpark economics (high-level) — assuming steady-state 230M/mo and private licensing model: 
- Licensing: One-time platform license plus annual platform fee. Ballpark: $60k–$120k one-time setup & license (based on environment/GPU count) + $48k–$120k/year platform fee for support and control plane (tier dependent).
- Unit inference economics (example): for private deployments we typically quote unit costs that combine reserved capacity cost + support/ops amortization. Roughly $700–$2,000 per 1M tokens served (this range depends heavily on quantization, model choice, instance type, and batching).
- For your 230M/mo that maps to ~ $161k–$460k/month if priced purely by token at those ranges — however, most private deals mix licensing + reserved capacity to reduce per-token cost (example: a reserved capacity commitment can bring unit to $200–$400 per 1M tokens).

Suggested next steps: 
- If the 300M is steady-state, we should size for reserved capacity (monthly commit) and propose a blended pricing target of $300–$450 per 1M tokens with a 12-month commit + a platform fee.
- If 300M is occasional peak, we can propose a smaller reserved baseline + burst pricing.

I've attached our Private Pricing overview + SOC2 checklist. Marissa (cc) will follow up with an environment/GPU sizing sketch and a concrete quote matrix (license + support tier + unit token buckets).

Would you like a 30m session tomorrow to review the quote matrix?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0199

Attachments: Redwood-Private-Pricing-Overview.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@medlytics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, priya.sharma@medlytics.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 13:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — pricing follow-up

Jordan — looping in some more concrete sizing and licensing options below. I'm a SE on the account; happy to refine after your answers to Aditya's Qs.

Sizing assumptions (initial proposal):
- Prod environment: 4x A10G equiv (or 2x H100 L3 80GB equiv depending on model/latency).
- Non-prod x2: each with 1x A10G equiv for validation/testing.
- KV/prefix cache expected to reduce effective cost by ~15–25% depending on prompt reuse.

Licensing & support model (common structure we use):
1) One-time license/setup by environment band: 
   - Small (1 env): $40k one-time
   - Medium (2–3 envs): $75k one-time
   - Large (4+ envs): $120k one-time
2) Annual platform fee (includes control plane, console, telemetry):
   - Standard support: $25k/year (business hours, 99.5% platform availability SLA)
   - Premium support: $60k/year (24x7, 99.9% SLA, named TAM, quarterly QBRs)
3) Reserved capacity commit (monthly billing) covering GPUs & throughput. Example blended reserved + support outcome: 
   - Modest commit (covers 100M tokens/mo): adds $15k/mo (~$150 per 1M tokens effective)
   - Mid commit (covers 300M tokens/mo): adds $40k/mo (~$133 per 1M tokens effective)
   - High commit (covers 1B tokens/mo): larger discounts apply; effective unit may go below $100 per 1M tokens depending on model/quantization.

Putting together a sample (for 230M/mo steady-state):
- One-time license: Medium band = $75k (one-time)
- Annual platform fee: Premium = $60k/year
- Reserved commit: mid = $40k/mo = $480k/year
- Effective token unit: ~ $174 per 1M tokens (blended: reserved + support amortized).

This shows how blended structures dramatically reduce the pure per-token list price I shared earlier. If you are targeting $/1M token goal in procurement, we typically aim for a blended target and show how license + reserved commitments get you there.

Questions for you: 
- Confirm 2 non-prod + 1 prod — is that correct? Any requirement for DR region or standby capacity?
- Any procurement constraints (PO terms, amortization over multiple years) we should model?

I can put together a 1-page pricing matrix with toggles for support tier and reserved commit levels. If helpful I can include an amortized 3-year TCO comparison vs hosted API pricing.

-M
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-Checklist.xlsx
